slides.say: The largest range of carbon percents is found in the samples from which planet?
What's a range? It's everything from the smallest value to the biggest one. Here it's carbon, so we look across.

slides: So for each planet, we take its leftmost sample and its rightmost sample. The range is the distance between them.
Do we read each number and subtract? No. We draw a line from the leftmost to the rightmost sample, and we compare the lengths by eye.

slides.say: Venus, the squares. From about ten to about thirty. A short line.
Saturn, the triangles. From about eight all the way to fifty-five. Much longer than Venus. So Venus is out.
Mars, the diamonds. From twenty to fifty. Shorter than Saturn's line. Out.
Neptune, the rings. From forty to seventy-four. Also shorter than Saturn's line. Out.
So Saturn has the largest range. We didn't calculate anything. We just compared lengths. That's one of the main ways we solve chart questions.
Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
